title: Policy
description: The one provider-neutral policy, .ai/repo/policy.yaml: budgets, verification, retention, enforcement and projections.

session.description: What the provider's episode events do beyond drawing the boundary: how much the start event hands the worker, and whether the compaction and end events record anything.

briefing_on_start.description: Hand the worker a briefing on the start event's standard output, which the provider adds to the context it is about to build. False restores the older silence, in which a continuation record is written and nothing loads it.

briefing_budget_lines.description: Hard cap on what the start event writes to the provider's context. Text that arrives in every episode is paid for in every episode.

checkpoint_on_compact.description: Record a derived checkpoint when the provider announces a compaction, and again when an episode closes. Both are moments at which what the episode knows stops being reachable. Neither asks whether a task is open: a checkpoint is the episode's record and a task is an optional relation it names when it has one (ADR 0052).

handover_on_end.description: Write a derived continuation record when an episode ends. Until ADR 0052 this happened only while a task was still active, so a repository whose last task had been handed over stopped writing the one record a future worker resumes from.

stranded_after.description: How long an open episode may go without a sign of life before `majordomus recover` may close it. The sign of life is the later of the episode's own started_at and the newest ledger line it stamped. Generous on purpose: closing a live episode costs the worker inside it the boundary of its work, and leaving a dead one open another hour costs nothing.

ensure_server_on_start.description: On the start event, make sure the repository's shared server serves this checkout (`majordomus serve ensure`): a server is started when none answers, never built, and the briefing names where it stands. False leaves the server to the first MCP client.

freshness.description: How old a continuation record may be before it stops being current. This is a different question from divergence (exact/advanced/diverged/different_context), which says where the record's commit sits relative to HEAD and nothing whatever about time: a record is `advanced` on the day it is written and still `advanced` a month later. Declared once here and read by every surface; a second copy of either number in a shell function, a Rust constant or a page of prose is the drift this file exists to prevent.

fresh_minutes.description: Below this age a record is `fresh`: current, act on it.

stale_minutes.description: At or beyond this age a record is `stale`: history, never presented as the current instruction. Between the two it is `aging` — still current, but its age is stated.

prompts.description: Bounds on the raw prompt archive under .ai/local/prompts/. Pruning replaces a prompt body with a tombstone and keeps every other field, including the provenance of its episode link; a record is never deleted. Either bound alone is a bound.

retention_max_days.description: A prompt body older than this many days is pruned.

retention_max_bytes.description: The total size of the prompt bodies the archive keeps; the oldest are pruned first past it.

commit.description: What a commit message is held to. The type vocabulary is not here: it is the changelog's own, and a second copy under this key is the duplication the commit subsystem exists to remove.

subject_max_chars.description: The widest a subject line may be, measured whole including the type and scope.

scope_unknown.description: A scope outside the vocabulary the repository's own history yields.

fix_requires_test.description: A `fix` whose files include no test.

reference_unresolved.description: A record id in the message that the layer does not hold.

breaking_unexplained.description: A commit marked breaking with no body and no BREAKING CHANGE trailer.

benchmark.description: How majordomus bench samples, and the thresholds bench --check and the command budgets apply.

doctor_ms.description: Wall-time budget for `majordomus doctor`; over it the command WARNs and still exits on its findings.

watch_ms.description: Wall-time budget for `majordomus watch`; over it the command WARNs and still exits on its findings.

enter_ms.description: Wall-time budget for entering the repository (`majordomus env enter`) when a server is already serving this checkout, which is every entry but the first. Entering a directory is something a person does dozens of times a day and never chose to wait for.

enter_cold_ms.description: Wall-time budget for the first entry, which additionally finds that nothing answers and starts a server — and then returns, because entry never waits for a server it started to become ready.

use_cases.description: How use-case coverage is gated: per class of target, whether a gap fails, is reported, or is not looked at.
